# Selective EGFR Inhibitor Design for NSCLC Research

## 1. Target Validation

**Target:** Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR / HER1)
**UniProt:** [P00533](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00533) (EGFR_HUMAN, 1210 aa, *Homo sapiens*)
**ChEMBL target:** CHEMBL203 (Single Protein — "Epidermal growth factor receptor")

Note on selectivity scope: ChEMBL also lists EGFR as part of multi-target family entries — CHEMBL2111431 (EGFR+ErbB2/HER1-HER2 pair) and CHEMBL2363049 (ErbB family: EGFR, ERBB2, ERBB3, ERBB4 — accessions P04626, Q15303, P21860). Since the goal here is a **selective** EGFR inhibitor, CHEMBL203 (single protein) is the correct primary target, and CHEMBL2363049 is the relevant counter-panel for assessing ErbB-family selectivity liability.

EGFR is one of the best-validated oncology targets in NSCLC: activating mutations (exon 19 deletions, L858R) drive a significant fraction of lung adenocarcinomas, and EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (gefitinib, erlotinib, afatinib, osimertinib) are standard-of-care in mutation-positive disease. The clinical challenge motivating continued design work is acquired resistance, most commonly via the T790M (and now C797S) gatekeeper mutations, plus off-target toxicity from wild-type EGFR inhibition in skin/gut and from cross-reactivity with other kinases.
